title: Prefetch negotiator and compact-quant advisor: heterogeneity-aware cache/quant defaults
author: Marcus Wu
ci_status: pass (build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-tests: flaky -> rerun passed, lint: pass, perf-regression: pass)
description: Motivation: production workloads show that naive prefix caching + one-size quant profiles underperform across heterogeneous batches and multi-tenant GPUs. This PR introduces a Prefetch Negotiator service and a Compact Quant Advisor to automatically suggest conservative caching and quantization defaults per workload class. Goals: reduce token-cost by improving cache utility without increasing tail latency; provide compact quant profiles that retain quality for short/interactive sessions; make defaults consultable and overridable via runtime config. Changes: - New component: prefetch-negotiator (runtime service) that observes sequence-length distribution, KV cache hit patterns, and per-model latency budget and decides prefetch budget (KB per-request), eviction hints, and negotiation tags for routing. - Compact Quant Advisor: offline analyzer that profiles small prompt sets (warmup + edge cases) and synthesizes 2-3 compact quant profiles (e.g., 4-bit FP+per-channel scale, int8 hybrid) ranked by cost/quality score. - Policy glue: config layer to apply negotiated cache budgets and recommended quant profile to a model-variant at rollout time with canary gating. - Metrics and tracepoints: added prefetch_hit_ratio, prefetch_cost_estimate, quant_advisor_quality_delta, and a dashboard template. - CLI/tooling: `rwd cost-suggester prefetch --workload <yaml>` and `rwd quant-advisor profile <model> --samples <n>`. Implementation notes: Prefetch Negotiator runs as a sidecar in serving pods and emits signed negotiation tokens that the router honors; negotiation is optimistic and falls back to existing cache behaviour on mismatch. Compact Quant Advisor uses representative samples + accuracy hook to generate quality delta estimates; we avoid re-training and rely on calibrated post-quantization evaluation. Backwards compatibility: defaults are non-breaking; operators can opt-in via runtime flags. Testing: unit + integration with synthetic workloads that exercise bursty short-seq traffic and long-seq streams; manual QA on staging with a canary serving 5% traffic for a week. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Perf benchmark + dashboard - [x] Docs/CLI help - [x] Security review (KMS tokens usage) Rollout plan: initial rollout behind runtime feature flag, enable negotiator for low-latency tiers only (SLO <= 150ms) and enable quant advisor suggestions as non-binding recommendations for 2 weeks, then automatic apply with canary if cost savings exceed threshold and quality delta < 1.5%.
